newsitem.title: CHINA: China replaces HK work visa with new entry card.
newsitem.headline: China replaces HK work visa with new entry card.

text.p: China has scrapped the use of passports by mainland residents working or studying in Hong Kong and will instead issue a special card allowing them to visit the territory, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.

The Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office of the State Council, or cabinet, had approved the new rules to be effective from July 1, the day Hong Kong saw the end of British colonial rule and became a special administrative region of China, Xinhua said.

Under the new rules, all residents of mainland China going to Hong Kong to study, train or work would have to get a "Permit of Passage to and from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region", the agency said.
Formerly, mainland residents staying in Hong Kong for an extended period had to obtain a Chinese passport as well as an entry visa from British authorities, it said.
Holders of such passports could exchange their visas for a transit permit before December 31 this year, it said.
China has vowed to strictly control migration from the mainland to Hong Kong under its "one country, two systems" government formula for the crowded former British colony.
